guard: every name the spawn auto-numbering can produce is a mintable mesh actor, and the name door refuses an unmintable name where it is chosen rather than at mint
why: The bug this pins was a COMPOSITION bug: both halves were individually correct. The numbering
produced a perfectly good display name, and the validator correctly refused a token containing
the separator it reserves. Nothing was wrong until one fed the other, which is why reading
either function alone finds nothing. So the cells compose the two SHIPPED functions in the same
order the manager composes them and hand the numbering's own output to the real validator —
rather than asserting a remembered alphabet, which would stay green if either side drifted.
M1 is the regression itself. M2 is the one that matters more for the long run: it changes the
separator to something ELSE that is still illegal in a token. A cell that merely asserted the
name is not the old `<base>-2` string would stay green; only handing it to the validator fails.
the validator. It is written to be CORRECT TODAY, so every behavioural cell stays green and only
the composition cell can see it. This is the drift the single-predicate design exists to
prevent, and the only honest way to pin it is a mutant that is currently harmless.
M3 severs the delegation — the door restates the alphabet as its own regex instead of calling the
validator. It is written to be CORRECT TODAY, so no behavioural cell can see it; it SURVIVED the
first run and the harness's positive control proved the file was loaded, so that was a genuine
coverage gap and not an unreachable mutant. It is killed structurally now. Worth stating plainly:
a rule that is only ever enforced by one call site cannot be pinned by behaviour, because a
faithful copy behaves identically until the day it stops — so the cell has to read the source.
M4 and M5 guard the two rules that must NOT move. M4 makes user mode accept a hyphen again
(the defect, at the door rather than in the numbering). M5 applies the narrow rule in static/open
mode too, which is the plausible over-correction: it looks stricter and safer, and it would break
every existing `my-agent` persona on upgrade for a constraint that does not apply there, since
that mode keys the actor on the minted nkey and never on the name.
M6 drops the traversal guard while keeping the token rule. The token alphabet happens to exclude
`/` and `.` anyway, so user mode stays safe and only the static/open half of each path-hostile
cell reddens — which is exactly the half that still has to hold.
V0 is the vacuity control and it mutates the SUITE rather than the source. It exists because the
first version of this suite compared its count to the loop variable that produced it, which is
satisfied at zero: 19 of 20 cells passed against an empty series. The floors are asserted against
a literal now. A count is only evidence when it cannot be met by measuring nothing.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. These cells drive the two exported functions directly, not a live manager.
The manager reaches them by delegation (`nameError` returns `spawnNameError(...)`) and by using
`firstFreeName` for its funnel; that wiring is one call each and is typechecked, but a live
spawn being refused end to end is NOT proven here and is named as a residual.

mutations.cell: instrument control: the collision series is NON-EMPTY (N names)
mutations.note: Mutates the SUITE, not the implementation — the question is whether these cells can be satisfied by measuring nothing. Every claim over `produced` is universal ('every name is mintable', 'all distinct', 'the door accepts every one') and a universal claim over an empty set is true. MEASURED, before the floors were added: 19 of 20 cells still passed with the series emptied, because the count was compared to SERIES itself — the same variable that produced it, which is satisfied at zero. Floors against a literal now redden 5 cells. Raised by the review lane, not by me; my own count assertion looked rigorous and was not.

mutations.expectRed: the narrow half CALLS the shipped validator
mutations.cell: the narrow half CALLS the shipped validator (delegation, not a restatement)
mutations.note: CORRECT TODAY — it reproduces the validator's current alphabet exactly, so every BEHAVIOURAL cell stays green. It first ran as a SURVIVOR, with the harness's positive control confirming the file was loaded, which made it a real coverage gap rather than an unreachable mutant. That is the finding: a restatement that is right today is indistinguishable from delegation today, and diverges only after someone changes the token grammar — the one moment nobody is reading this door.
